value.overview: The Plain-breasted Ground Dove (Columbina minuta) is a very small dove that spends much of its time walking or feeding on the ground. It has plain, warm brown plumage and lacks the strongly scaled breast pattern of the Common Ground Dove. The species inhabits open, often seasonally dry country rather than dense forest. Its broad distribution extends from southern Mexico through Central America and across parts of northern and eastern South America.
value.classification: The Plain-breasted Ground Dove belongs to the dove and pigeon family Columbidae. It is one of several small ground doves in the genus Columbina.
value.identification: This is a tiny, compact ground dove with a short bill, short tail, and rounded wings. Adults are generally warm brown above and paler below, with relatively plain breast and belly plumage. The wings may show richer rufous or cinnamon tones in flight. Compared with the Common Ground Dove, it is smaller-looking and lacks the latter's obvious dark, scaled breast pattern. Sexes are similar, although males may appear slightly richer or more contrasting.
value.rangeHabitat: The species occurs from southern Mexico and Belize through Central America, then in separated regions of northern and eastern South America. In Costa Rica it is a local native bird, recorded mainly in open habitats of the drier northwest, especially Guanacaste, but it also occurs locally in parts of the central highlands and has been recorded near Turrialba. It uses dry or seasonally wet grassland, scrub, brushy second growth, agricultural edges, and other open lowland or lower-elevation habitats, generally avoiding dense forest.
value.migrationStatus: Generally resident in Costa Rica. Local or seasonal movements may occur, but it is not normally treated as a regular long-distance migrant there.
value.breeding: The Plain-breasted Ground Dove is believed to breed in suitable parts of its range, including Central America and Costa Rica, although detailed information on its breeding biology is limited. Like other small Columbina doves, it is expected to place a simple platform nest of twigs in low vegetation, shrubs, or similar cover. Clutches are usually small, and both adults typically share incubation and care of the young. Breeding timing may vary with rainfall and local food availability.
value.dietFeeding: It feeds mainly on small seeds and other plant material collected from the ground. Foraging usually takes place in open areas, where the dove walks quietly through short grass, bare soil, scrub margins, fields, and disturbed ground. It may forage alone, in pairs, or in small groups. Grain-producing plants and naturally available seeds become especially important in seasonally dry landscapes.
value.behavior: This discreet ground dove usually walks rather than flies while searching for food and may remain concealed in grass or low cover. When disturbed, it makes a quick, direct flight and often drops back into vegetation nearby. It is generally unobtrusive and may be overlooked among other small doves. Courtship and social behavior are likely most noticeable during the breeding season, when pairs defend small areas and perform display flights or postures.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not well documented, but the species is not currently considered to be undergoing a major global decline.
